title: How to Build a Recession Proof Portfolio: 8 Smart Moves for 2026
summary: List every account, then check your mix, concentration, fees and goals. Rebalance only if something drifted. A yearly review is enough for most.
body_markdown:
## How Astor fits into a portfolio review


Astor is a personal investing agent on iPhone and in iMessage. It connects to brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts at most major US institutions, such as Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase, through Plaid, so the first step of a review, getting your accounts into one picture, is done once instead of every year. Astor can see your holdings but can’t move money, and you don’t transfer anything to it.


Between reviews, Astor follows every position you own and the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them, and texts you when something crosses a line you care about.[At a glance](https://www.astor.app/blog/at-a-glance) gives you a five-second daily check with two lines on what moved your money today and why. Themes let you group what you own, like AI infrastructure or nuclear power, and follow each group, which can help you notice when several holdings ride on the same idea. With[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) , you can ask Astor to check something on a schedule, like every Monday morning or before a company you own reports, and the free plan includes one custom alert. You can also ask Astor questions about your actual holdings in the app or[in iMessage](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) .


Astor doesn’t rebalance, trade or decide anything in your connected accounts, and it doesn’t do tax filing or estate planning. The AI can be wrong, which is why it shows its sources. You make every decision. Astor is free to start and available in the US only, and you can[see how it works](https://www.astor.app/#how-it-works) .
